extra.message: The user-supplied registration code (form.registration_code.data) is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string via an f-string passed to sqlalchemy.text() and executed with session.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the 'registration_code' field of the signup form, enabling authentication/registration bypass and data exfiltration.

The 'search' query parameter (request.args.get('search')) is concatenated into a raw SQL LIKE clause via an f-string passed to sqlalchemy.text(). This raw fragment is combined into the query filter and executed, allowing SQL injection through the /search endpoint's 'search' parameter.

The 'preferences' cookie value is base64-decoded and passed directly to pickle.loads() in the before_request handler. Pickle deserialization of attacker-controlled data leads to arbitrary code execution (RCE), since an attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload in the cookie. The cookie is also produced via pickle.dumps in /darkmode (line 105) and after_request (line 128).

In the 404 error handler, request.path (attacker-controlled URL path) is embedded into an f-string and passed to render_template_string(). Jinja2 will evaluate template syntax in the attacker-controlled string, resulting in Server-Side Template Injection that can lead to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Server-Side Template Injection / Code Injection

extra.message: download() passes a user-supplied URL (from the profile image form via /account/image) directly to urllib.request.urlopen() with no validation of scheme or host. An attacker can supply internal URLs (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost) or file:// URIs, causing Server-Side Request Forgery and potential local file disclosure (the result is base64-encoded and stored/displayed).

The /accounts/<user_id>/notes endpoint returns all notes belonging to the user_id given in the URL without checking that user_id matches the authenticated user. Any logged-in user can enumerate user_id values and read other users' private notes (Insecure Direct Object Reference / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: update_account() blindly merges all submitted form fields into current_user.__dict__ (mass assignment). The AccountForm includes an 'is_admin' BooleanField, so a user can submit is_admin=true and escalate to administrator. It also allows overwriting arbitrary user attributes such as email. This is a privilege-escalation / broken access control flaw.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The POST /account (update_account) route has no @login_required decorator, unlike the other account routes. It operates on current_user but lacks authentication enforcement, allowing the account-update logic (including the is_admin mass-assignment) to be reached without proper authentication checks.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: delete_note() looks up the note by the note_id from the URL and deletes it without verifying that the note belongs to the current user (or that the user is an admin). Any authenticated user can delete any other user's note by guessing/iterating note IDs (broken access control / IDOR).

Note text is rendered with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter, disabling auto-escaping. Note text is user-supplied (NoteForm.text) and stored unsanitized, so a stored Cross-Site Scripting payload in a note's text will execute in the browsers of all users viewing the home page (notes can be public/shared).

Flask app.secret_key is hardcoded to a weak, publicly known value ('super secret key'). This key signs session cookies and Flask-Login 'remember me' tokens; knowing it lets an attacker forge session cookies and impersonate any user, including admins.

A static, hardcoded registration code ('a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764') is seeded into the database. Anyone who knows this value (it is committed to source) can self-register an account, bypassing the intended invite-only registration control.

The SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, which logs all executed SQL statements (including parameter values) to stderr. In production this exposes sensitive data and query structure in logs (information disclosure).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The 'preferences' cookie (which is later deserialized with pickle) is set without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite flags. Combined with the pickle deserialization sink, this weakens cookie protection; the cookie is also set in after_request (line 127-128) with the same insecure configuration.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without Secure Attribute / CWE-1004
